macros.name: APACciteatitle
macros.doc: \APACciteatitle determines the formatting of the title of an article (or similar work) when used as a citation in the text when no author or editor is available for that purpose.

macros.name: APACmetastar
macros.doc: \APACmetastar is the asterisk that precedes an item in the bibliography to denote that it is included in the meta-analysis.

macros.name: APACmonth
macros.doc: The \APACmonth command translates the numbers to the month or season names.

macros.name: APACrefauthstyle
macros.doc: \APACrefauthstyle is similar to \BAstyle, except that this one is used for formatting authors in the reference list.

macros.name: authorindexname
macros.doc: Name (heading) of the author index.

macros.name: BAnd
macros.doc: The third “and”, \BAnd, is used in the reference list if someone is both editor and translator: “In J. Strachey (Ed. & Trans.),”.

macros.name: BAP
macros.doc: \BAP is inserted after the prefix and before the first citation in a parenthetical citation.

macros.name: BAstyle
macros.doc: \BAstyle defines the text style of the authors (or whatever takes their place) for an in-text citation.

macros.name: BAuthor
macros.doc: \BAuthor “Author” as a description of the publisher if the author and publisher are the same.

macros.name: BBAA
macros.doc: \BBAA is the “and” between authors in a parenthetical citation and in the reference list, as in “(Mooijaart & Bentler, 1986)” or “Mooijaart, A., & Bentler, P. M. (1986).”.

macros.name: BBAB
macros.doc: \BBAB is the same “and” in a text citation, as in “Mooijaart and Bentler (1986)”.

macros.name: BBAY
macros.doc: \BBAY is the punctuation between author(s) and year in a parenthetical citation, as in “(Rao, 1973)”.

macros.name: BBC
macros.doc: \BBC is the punctuation between multiple cites, as in “(Rao, 1973; Mooijaart & Bentler, 1986)”.

macros.name: BBCP
macros.doc: \BBOP (opening parenthesis) and \BBCP (closing parenthesis) are used for the parentheses in a citation, as in “(Rao, 1973)” or “Rao (1973)”, and the year in the reference list, as in “Rao, C. R. (1973).”

macros.name: BBN
macros.doc: \BBN is the punctuation before a note (postfix) after a citation, as in “(Rao, 1973, p. 25)”.

macros.name: BBOP
macros.doc: \BBOP (opening parenthesis) and \BBCP (closing parenthesis) are used for the parentheses in a citation, as in “(Rao, 1973)” or “Rao (1973)”, and the year in the reference list, as in “Rao, C. R. (1973).”

macros.name: Bby
macros.doc: \Bby “by” in the construction “by P. R. Krishnaiah, Ed.” referring to the original editor of a reprinted work.

macros.name: BBYY
macros.doc: \BBYY is the punctuation between two subsequent years, if two works by the same author(s) are referenced in a single citation command, as in “(Rao, 1965, 1973)” or “Rao (1965, 1973)”.

macros.name: BCBT
macros.doc: \BCBT is the comma between authors in the reference section when there are two authors, as in “Mooijaart, A., & Bentler, P. M. (1986).”

macros.name: BCHAIR
macros.doc: Chair of a symposium, etc. Default is “Chair”.

macros.name: BCHAP
macros.doc: Used for incollection if the pages field is empty, to denote the chapter number of the referenced work in the collection.

macros.name: BDBL
macros.doc: \BDBL is the dots before the last author in the reference section when the reference has more than seven authors.

macros.name: BEd
macros.doc: Edition, as in “2nd ed.”.

macros.name: BED
macros.doc: Editor in reference list, as in “In P. R. Krishnaiah (Ed.)”.

macros.name: BEDS
macros.doc: Editors (more than one editor) in reference list, as in “In C. R. Rao & J. K. Ghosh (Eds.)”.

macros.name: BHBI
macros.doc: \BHBI is the hyphen between initials.

macros.name: bibcorporate
macros.doc: This command can be used in the author field (and editor and translator) to tell apacite that the author is a corporate author.

macros.name: bibitemsep
macros.doc: \bibitemsep gives the vertical separation between two reference list entries.

macros.name: biblabelsep
macros.doc: \biblabelsep gives the horizontal separation between the reference list label and the rest of the entry.

macros.name: bibleftmargin
macros.doc: \bibleftmargin gives the indentation of the second and subsequent lines of a reference list entry, relative to the usual left margin.

macros.name: bibliographyprenote
macros.doc: This command is used before the reference list, but after the section or chapter heading, and immediately after \bibliographytypesize. It is intended for an optional note just before the references in the reference list.

macros.name: bibname
macros.doc: Name of the reference list if it’s a chapter.

macros.name: bibnodate
macros.doc: Used in the year and originalyear fields to indicate that no publication date has been given.

macros.name: bibnotype
macros.doc: It is used for techreport entries to indicate that the type specifier should be suppressed.

macros.name: BIP
macros.doc: “In press”, the string to be used as year for in-press references.

macros.name: BMsgPostedTo
macros.doc: Used for messages to newsgroups and the like.

macros.name: BMTh
macros.doc: The (default) master’s thesis type name, which can be overridden by the type field.

macros.name: BOthers
macros.doc: Used for “others” if the number of authors or editors is too large, as in “(Gill et al., 1981)”.

macros.name: BPBI
macros.doc: \BPBI is the period between initials.

macros.name: BPhD
macros.doc: The (default) PhD thesis type name, which can be overridden by the type field.

macros.name: BRetrievedFrom
macros.doc: “Retrieved from”, used if the url field is specified but the lastchecked field is not.

macros.name: BTR
macros.doc: The (default) technical report type name, which can be overridden by the type field.

macros.name: BUMTh
macros.doc: The (default) unpublished master’s thesis type name, which can be overridden by the type field.

macros.name: BUPhD
macros.doc: The (default) Unpublished PhD thesis type name, which can be overridden by the type field.

macros.name: BVOL
macros.doc: Volume, as in “Vol. 1”.

macros.name: cite
macros.doc: The traditional LaTeX citation command is \cite, and apacite reimplements this command. This command is used for parenthetical citations.

macros.name: citeauthorp
macros.doc: For consistency with \citep and \citet, when loaded with the natbibapa option, apacite defines \citeauthorp for parenthetical use and \citeauthort for text use, and the corresponding capitalized versions \Citeauthorp and \Citeauthort.

macros.name: Citeauthorp
macros.doc: For consistency with \citep and \citet, when loaded with the natbibapa option, apacite defines \citeauthorp for parenthetical use and \citeauthort for text use, and the corresponding capitalized versions \Citeauthorp and \Citeauthort.

macros.name: citeauthort
macros.doc: For consistency with \citep and \citet, when loaded with the natbibapa option, apacite defines \citeauthorp for parenthetical use and \citeauthort for text use, and the corresponding capitalized versions \Citeauthorp and \Citeauthort.

macros.name: Citeauthort
macros.doc: For consistency with \citep and \citet, when loaded with the natbibapa option, apacite defines \citeauthorp for parenthetical use and \citeauthort for text use, and the corresponding capitalized versions \Citeauthorp and \Citeauthort.

macros.name: citeyear
macros.doc: The \citeyear command gives just the year part of a text citation.

macros.name: citeyearNP
macros.doc: The \citeyearNP command (NP = no parentheses) omits the parentheses, which can be useful for a construction like “In \citeyearNP{Jone01}, \citeauthor{Jone01} introduced his method”, which gives “In 2001, Jones introduced his method”.

macros.name: corporateAX
macros.doc: Depending on whether the suppresscorporate option or the includecorporate option is requested, either explicitly or implicitly, \corporateAX either swallows its argument or is equivalent to \AX.

macros.name: doiprefix
macros.doc: String that is printed before a DOI.

macros.name: url
macros.doc: The url package provides the \url command for formatting URLs, i.e., web addresses.

envs.name: APACrefauthors
envs.doc: Formatting of authors (or editors acting as authors) in the reference list.
